findings.title: Possible NPE when the all-clients resource is missing
findings.body: `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)` falls back to `getResourceTypeResource(...)` when the client has no specific resource. That method can return null, for example in realms whose admin-permissions client was initialized before the Clients type was added to the schema. The null resource is then passed straight to `findByResource`, and later `resource.getScopes()` is dereferenced. The result is a NullPointerException, which surfaces as a 500 error, instead of a plain denial.

findings.title: canMapRoles and related checks ignore MANAGE_CLIENTS role and per-client manage
findings.body: `canMapRoles`, `canMapCompositeRoles` and `canMapClientScopeRoles` only evaluate the specific scope. They do not check whether the caller has the manage-clients admin role or the manage scope, which the V1 behaviour and other V2 methods honour. As a result, admins holding the manage-clients role lose the ability to map roles, which is a regression.

findings.title: Removal listener now runs only when the V1 feature flag is on, but still dispatches to V2
findings.body: The listener is now gated on `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` (V1). However, `management()` still returns `MgmtPermissionsV2` whenever V2 is enabled. If both features are enabled, a client removal event calls `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled`, which throws `UnsupportedOperationException` and breaks client deletion. In addition, V2 resources for deleted clients or users are never cleaned up.

findings.title: getClientsWithPermission relies on resource type that per-client resources don't have
findings.body: `getOrCreateResource` creates per-client resources without setting their type; only the all-clients resource has type Clients. As a result, `findByType` returns only the "Clients" resource, so `granted` contains the string "Clients" instead of client IDs. Per-client grants are therefore never listed.

findings.title: getResourceName not updated for Clients type
findings.body: For the Clients resource type, `getResourceName` falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()`. That value is null or the raw client UUID, unlike Users, which resolves to a readable username. Permission listings therefore show unhelpful resource names for client permissions.
